stem: White material is observed on leaves, but no diagnostic structures have been confirmed. What is the best next step before a disease-specific response?
choices: Classify the material as powdery mildew because white foliar growth is sufficiently characteristic to justify a disease-specific response.
Begin a broad fungicide response while collecting confirmation, because delaying treatment creates more risk than treating a possible false positive.
Examine representative material, compare look-alikes, and obtain confirmation appropriate to the consequence before making a disease-specific decision.
Prioritize environmental correction first because white foliar material is more likely to be residue or stress when no diagnostic structures are visible.
rationale: White foliar material can be consistent with powdery mildew, but color and gross appearance alone are not enough to establish a specific disease. Residues, mineral deposits, spray artifacts, trichomes, debris, and other non-disease conditions can create look-alikes. The strongest next step is to examine representative material and use confirmation proportional to the consequence of the decision while maintaining appropriate containment/escalation. Treating first or dismissing disease first both collapse the differential before the evidence supports that choice.
